title: A birational group law over a trait has a finite-type group envelope
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $E=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fibres and products mean scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. A group scheme over a base has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over that base satisfying the group identities (the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with the indicated base in place of a field). Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An open $U\subseteq Y$ of a $T$-scheme is $T$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for both $s\in T$. A $T$-rational map is an equivalence class of morphisms on $T$-dense opens, where representatives agree on a $T$-dense open of their common domain. A $T$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $T$-dense open subschemes. Let $Y$ be a smooth separated finite-type $T$-scheme with nonempty special fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and identify $Y_E$ with a smooth finite-type $E$-group scheme $G$. Suppose multiplication on $G$ extends to a $T$-rational map $m:Y\times_TY\dashrightarrow Y$, defined on the entire generic fibre, whose universal translations $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$ are $T$-birational self-maps of $Y\times_TY$, and which is associative wherever the two composites are defined. Then there is a smooth separated finite-type $T$-group scheme $M$ and an open immersion $j:Y\hookrightarrow M$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with $T$-dense image such that $j_E:Y_E\to M_E$ is an isomorphism of $E$-group schemes, and multiplication on $M$ restricts to $m$. No mapping property for $M$ is asserted.

source.place: BLR 4.3 Theorem 6, printed p.108 (PDF p.114), equivalently 5.1 Theorem 5 including the no-shrinking clause, printed p.114 (PDF p.120). Primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply strictification to $(Y,m)$ and choose a $T$-dense open $U\subseteq Y$ containing $Y_E$ on which the law is strict. Realize this strict law as a $T$-dense open immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow M$ into a smooth separated finite-type $T$-group scheme. These lemmas apply because both fibres of $Y$ are nonempty and its generic law is the given group law.

Over $E$, the pairs $(M_E,i_E)$ and $(G,\mathrm{id})$ both realize the strict law on $U_E=Y_E=G$. Uniqueness in the field case gives an $E$-group isomorphism $a:M_E\simeq G$ with $a i_E=\mathrm{id}$. In particular $i_E$ is an isomorphism, so the morphism $i$ on $U$ already has the required entire generic fibre.

The codimension-one assertion for smooth trait models shows that $U$ contains every point $y$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}\leq1$. Apply the existing relative Weil extension theorem to $D=R$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X=Y$, target $M$ and $i:U\to M$: $U$ is dense in each fibre and contains all those points. Its base hypotheses hold: a DVR is a Noetherian domain of dimension one, and it is integrally closed since in a monic integral equation a fraction of negative valuation has its highest power of strictly smaller valuation than every other term, an impossibility. Obtain a morphism $j:Y\to M$ extending $i$.

Apply the immersion criterion with $X=Y$, $Z=M$, $f=j$ and the same $U$. Its generic map is $i_E$, an isomorphism, and $j|_U=i$ is an open immersion. Thus $j$ is an open immersion. Its image is $T$-dense because it contains the already $T$-dense open $i(U)$. Its generic map is the group isomorphism of step 2.

source.place: 5.1 Theorem 5, differential determinant and open immersion

proof.text: On any open domain $D\subseteq Y\times_TY$ representing $m$, the two morphisms $j m$ and $\mu_M(j\times j)$ to $M$ agree on $D_E$, by step 2. Apply the uniqueness clause of rational spreading with base $Z=T$, smooth source $Y\times_TY$ and smooth separated target $M$ to conclude equality on $D$. The source is smooth by smooth base change and composition. Consequently multiplication restricts to the given rational law, including its chosen representatives. This proves all requested clauses.
